--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_sudoku_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add the Sudoku graph of order n: the cells of an n\^2 x n\^2 Sudoku grid, joined when twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_sudoku_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Add the Sudoku graph of order n: the cells of an n\^2 x n\^2 Sudoku grid, joined when title: >- [Graph.add_sudoku_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add the Sudoku graph of order n: the cells of an n\^2 x n\^2 Sudoku grid, joined when page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add the Sudoku graph of order `n`: the cells of an `n^2 x n^2` Sudoku grid, joined when ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20102-L20249){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_sudoku_graph( n=3, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} they can't hold the same digit. ![Sudoku graph](../assets/graphs/add-sudoku-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The 4 by 4 Sudoku graph for n=2 three times, drawn as its grid with a small gap between the 2 by 2 boxes and, in each panel, only the edges of one cell shown, in the accent color. Each cell is joined to the other cells in its row, its column, and its box, seven in all, so a valid Sudoku solution is a proper four-coloring of the graph. Edges along a row or column bow around the cells in between." width="100%"} Creates one node per cell of an `n^2 x n^2` grid (81 cells for the usual `n = 3`), row by row, and joins two cells when they share a row, a column or an `n x n` box. Solving a Sudoku puzzle is exactly finding a proper coloring of this graph with `n^2` colors (the digits) that extends the given clues, so the graph turns puzzles into graph coloring problems. Every cell has `3 n^2 - 2 n - 1` neighbors (20 for `n = 3`), giving `n^4 (3 n^2 - 2 n - 1) / 2` edges (810 for `n = 3`). Orders `0` and `1` have no edges. It is NetworkX's `sudoku_graph()`. With `label=True` each cell is labelled `"(row,col)"`, counting from zero. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier cell (in row-by-row order) to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Sudoku graphs are useful for: - solving and analyzing Sudoku and Latin-square puzzles with coloring algorithms - test graphs with known chromatic number (`n^2`) and many large cliques - teaching graph coloring with a familiar example ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Order of the puzzle: the boxes are `n x n` and the grid `n^2 x n^2`. Default is `3` (the standard 9 x 9 Sudoku). Must be non-negative. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each cell is labelled with its zero-based position as `"(row,col)"`. Because these labels don't depend on the existing nodes, adding a second labelled grid raises `ValueError`; pass `label=False` for it. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~clique_number`) : Find the size of the largest clique, nine for a 9 x 9 grid. [](`~greedy_color`) : Color the cells so that no two neighbors share a digit. [](`~cartesian_product`) : Build the rook's graph, the Sudoku graph without its boxes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The standard Sudoku graph has 81 cells, each with 20 neighbors: ::: {#abeadbbb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_sudoku_graph() degrees = set(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values()) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), degrees ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (81, 810, {20}) ``` ::: ::: Each row, column and box is a clique of nine cells, so at least nine digits are needed, and a completed Sudoku shows nine are enough: ::: {#1feaebb3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9 ``` ::: ::: The 4 x 4 puzzle (`n=2`) is small enough to see a cell's neighbors: its row, its column and the rest of its box: ::: {#7d4c11ee .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} small = ec.Graph().add_sudoku_graph(n=2) sorted(small.get_label_from_id(v) for v in small.get_neighbors("(0,0)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['(0,1)', '(0,2)', '(0,3)', '(1,0)', '(1,1)', '(2,0)', '(3,0)'] ``` ::: ::: ### With boxes or without The 4 x 4 Sudoku graph on the left and the rook's graph on the right, the product of two complete graphs on four nodes, where cells are joined only along rows and columns. Both are drawn as the grid, with the top-left cell's edges picked out. The Sudoku graph adds one diagonal inside each box, `8` edges in all: ::: {#83a5858c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} k4 = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(4) rook = k4.cartesian_product(k4) def on_grid(g): pos = {v: ((v - 1) % 4, -((v - 1) // 4)) for v in g.get_node_ids()} return g.set_node_attrs("pos", pos) small.count_edges(), rook.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (56, 48) ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#f04126b9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} on_grid(small).plot( layout="pos", show_labels=False, node_size=7, highlight=[(1, v) for v in small.get_neighbors(1)], width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
